items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Ferguson became one of my best friends

ctx.x: By all means. And that's the way it was. We played all through that territory and Mr. Ferguson became one of my best friends, he took me out -- the first golf ball I ever hit in my life, he taught me how to hold a club. C. Ferguson, A very fine person and a very smart business man.

We rehearsed almost everyday, that's all we had to do was just hang around and rehearse, and all my spare time was spent in the library, I would go to the library and read everyday. That was my hobby, just reading, reading. Trying to learn, trying to pick up this. Read, read, read. We had a chance to make some records for the Gennett people. And we drove up to Richmond, Indiana am I right, Charles?
